message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
### ECG Interpretation

#### 1. Standardization & Technical Quality
* **Paper Speed:** 25 mm/s
* **Voltage Calibration:** 10 mm/mV (standard calibration mark of 10 mm / 1 mV is visible on the left)

---

#### 2. Rate & Rhythm
* **Rhythm:** Normal Sinus Rhythm (regular, upright P waves before every QRS in leads I, II; inverted in aVR; constant PR intervals).
* **Heart Rate:** ~**58–60 bpm** (R–R interval is ~5.0–5.2 large boxes; 10 beats across the 10-second Lead II rhythm strip).

---

#### 3. Intervals & Axis
* **PR Interval:** Normal (~160 ms / 4 small squares).
* **QRS Duration:** Normal / narrow (~80–90 ms).
* **QRS Axis:** **Left Axis Deviation (LAD)** (~-30° to -40°)
  * Lead I is predominantly positive (tall R wave).
  * Lead aVF and Lead III are predominantly negative.
  * Lead II is borderline/slightly biphasic.
* **QT / QTc:** ~420–440 ms (normal to mildly prolonged in precordial leads with deep T-wave inversions).

---

#### 4. Waveform & Morphology Analysis

* **P Waves:** Normal morphology and amplitude.
* **QRS Complexes:**
  * **Pathological Q waves / QS complexes** across **V1–V4** with loss of normal anterior R-wave progression.
  * Tall R wave in aVL; poor R wave development in V1–V4.
* **ST Segments & T Waves:**
  * **V1:** Mild ST elevation (~1–1.5 mm) with an inverted T wave.
  * **V2:** Marked convex (coved) **ST-segment elevation (~7–8 mm)** followed by terminal T-wave inversion.
  * **V3:** Marked convex (coved) **ST-segment elevation (~7–8 mm)** with deep T-wave inversion.
  * **V4:** Mild-to-moderate ST elevation (~1–2 mm) with **deep, symmetric T-wave inversion** (~5 mm depth).
  * **V5–V6:** Low T-wave amplitude / flat in V5, normal upright T wave in V6.
  * **Limb leads:** Isoelectric ST segments; no marked reciprocal depression.

---

### Diagnostic Impression

1. **Evolving Anterior / Anteroseptal ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)**
   * **Territory:** Left Anterior Descending (LAD) coronary artery.
   * **Key Findings:** 
     * QS pattern in V1–V4 indicates transmural infarction / myocardial necrosis.
     * Pronounced coved ST elevation in V1–V4 (most severe in V2–V3) indicates significant ongoing myocardial injury.
     * Deep T-wave inversion combined with persistent ST elevation is characteristic of the **subacute / evolving phase** (or reperfusion / late presentation) of an anterior STEMI.

2. **Differential Considerations:**
   * **Left Ventricular Aneurysm:** Chronic persistent ST-segment elevation with QS complexes persisting weeks to months following a prior anterior myocardial infarction.
   * **Takotsubo (Stress) Cardiomyopathy:** Can occasionally present with marked precordial ST elevation and deep T-wave inversions mimicking anterior STEMI.

> [!CAUTION]
> **Clinical Urgency:** If this is from an acute setting, this represents a **critical finding** requiring emergent clinical correlation (symptoms, vital signs, troponins) and urgent cardiology / catheterization laboratory evaluation.
